Volumes and scaling

Source: vignettes/volumes-scaling.Rmd
volumes-scaling.Rmd

stem_volume() calculates volume between stem bounds. tree_cubic_volume() returns the physical volume of selected logs. The example currency is United States dollars (USD). Product measurements are stored separately in gross_scale and net_scale.

Stem and log volume 

## Calculate volume from stump to a specified inside-bark top
volumes <- example_trees %>%
  transmute(tree,
            stem_cubic = stem_volume(dbh = dbh,
                                     ht = ht,
                                     model = model,
                                     upper = 6,
                                     upper_type = 'dib'))
tree stem_cubic
1 15.003
2 26.626
3 37.564
4 57.969
5 74.422
6 135.229 
## Calculate physical log volume under the example specifications
log_volumes <- example_trees %>%
  transmute(tree,
            log_cubic = tree_cubic_volume(dbh = dbh,
                                          ht = ht,
                                          species = species,
                                          model = model,
                                          products = example_products(name = 'pnw')))
tree log_cubic
1 16.574
2 27.939
3 39.005
4 59.240
5 75.765
6 136.586

stem_volume() accepts height, inside-bark diameter, outside-bark diameter, stump, or tip bounds. Its default interval runs from the model’s stump height to the tip. Physical log volume includes trim. Product scaling uses nominal length and excludes trim.

Measurement fields

volume_unit selects Scribner, International, Doyle, cubic volume, green tons, or cords. inside_bark sets acceptance diameter basis. Cubic and cord measurements use that bark basis.

Board-foot measurements use inside bark. Green weight includes wood and attached bark.

split_scale selects whole-log or section scaling for Scribner. It creates measurement sections without additional physical cuts. round selects default, downward, nearest-inch, or unrounded diameter preprocessing. The underlying board-foot procedure retains its prescribed internal rounding.

## Select a shipped tree
tree <- example_trees %>%
  filter(tree == 5)
tree spcd species dbh ht model
5 202 Douglas-fir 20 100 F00FW2W202 
## Load the example specifications
specifications <- example_products(name = 'douglas_fir')
product lengths min_length max_length min_sed trim volume_unit
Large sawlog 32 NA NA 12 0.5 scribner
Medium sawlog 16 NA NA 10 0.5 scribner
Small sawlog 16 NA NA 6 0.5 scribner
Pulp 8 20 3 0.5 green_ton 
## Select logs from the tree
result <- merchandise(dbh = tree$dbh,
                      ht = tree$ht,
                      model = tree$model,
                      species = tree$species,
                      id = tree$tree,
                      products = specifications,
                      currency = 'USD',
                      status = TRUE,
                      report_also = c('smalian', 'huber', 'international', 'doyle'))
log product nominal_length sed_ib net_scale scale_unit

2 Medium sawlog 16 11.643 80.000 board_foot
3 Small sawlog 16 8.413 40.000 board_foot
4 Pulp 20 3.341 0.098 green_short_ton 
## Select additional measurements on the existing cuts
measurements <- result$scales %>%
  filter(!is_product) %>%
  select(log, scale_rule, gross, net, unit, bark_basis)

report_also measures existing cuts with additional procedures. It does not change product acceptance or bucking.

Smalian and Huber reports use the nominal log body. Named definitions support fixed units and additional rounding operators. Scaling rules map product fields to measurement procedures.

Green tons follow the call’s units: short tons for imperial and metric tons for metric. Cord measurement requires cord_solid_fraction. green_weight() converts cubic volume to weight.
